text:
anika: quick follow-up to the weights-loader RFC — I'm worried about startup perf if we keep doing sequential shard reads for large models. can we discuss a parallel prefetch + coherence strategy?

matt: +1, saw a 3x variance on QPS during cold starts last week. idea: spawn N prefetch workers per device that read non-overlapping shards, verify hashes, then hand off mapped regions to the runtime.

lee: the challenge is disk contention and measurability. on nvme farm we can be aggressive, but on network filesystems prefetch floods cause timeouts. we need per-backend policies.

anika: agreed. proposal sketch: 1) manifest with shard ranges + hash + preferred backend hints 2) prefetcher that limits concurrency per backend and respects device-level inflight tokens 3) atomic swap when all required shards for a partition are ready

sam: that manifest idea is good. can we include a small schema? e.g.:

```
{
  "model": "gpt-13b",
  "shards": [ {"id":0, "path":"s3://.../shard-0.safetensors", "hash":"sha256:...", "offset":0}, ... ],
  "backend_hints": {"s3":"max_concurrency=4","nfs":"max_concurrency=1"}
}
```

matt: also add `warmup_priority` per shard so tiny layers (embeddings) are hotloaded earlier. that reduced latency for our chat endpoint in the sim.

lee: tradeoffs: 1) more memory pressure if we prefetch aggressively 2) complexity in failure modes (partial prefetch + node crash) 3) need a clear ownership model for mmapped pages vs runtime allocator

anika: ownership model we discussed in RFC v2: loader v3 API surface should expose `claim_region(shard_id)` and `release_region(shard_id)`. runtime asks for claim then maps into device address space. if prefetcher wins the claim, runtime gets zero-copy.

sam: what about safetensors vs legacy .pt? safetensors is faster to mmap and safe for partial reads. fallback path should still validate and convert on-the-fly but behind a slower path. maybe keep a `convert_cache` for converted safetensor blobs to reduce repeated conversions.

matt: on conversion cache: need eviction policy and strong versioning. if model version updates, stale converted blobs must be invalidated. manifest should include `format_version` and `source_digest`.

lee: one more: warmup priming of kv-cache. we should support an optional `kv_warmup` payload for the most common prefixes (few tokens) that the prefetcher can push into device memory after mapping weights. would cut 20-40ms in our bench for long-context prompts.

anika: nice. small API pledge: `Loader.load(model_manifest, opts={concurrency:..., prefetch:true, kv_warmup:[...], priority:...})` and events via infra-bot: `prefetch_started`, `shard_ready`, `load_complete`, with metrics `prefetch_time_ms`, `hash_verify_failures`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: prefetch_started for model=gpt-13b, run_id=2026-06-04T12:33: expected_shards=32

sam: rollout plan: implement prefetcher as an optional opt-in behind a feature flag. test on a small fleet of dedicated nodes with mirrors on local NVMe. gather metrics for tail latency and disk IOPS.

matt: can we also consider progressive warmup: start execution with first N layers loaded and stream later layers? reduces tail but complicates attention kv lifecycle.

lee: progressive is doable if runtime supports incremental graph/weights binding. that suggests adding `bind_shard_to_context(shard_id, ctx)` to the interface. long-term refactor but high upside for large models.

anika: action items: 1) sam to draft manifest schema + conversion cache RFC (due EOW) 2) matt to prototype prefetch worker that honors backend hints (POC next week) 3) lee to write failure-mode doc (partial prefetch + crash) 4) I'll update loader v3 API in the original RFC with `claim_region` and `bind_shard_to_context`.

sam: noted. also will add perf knobs: `max_inflight_bytes_per_backend` and `per_device_prefetch_workers` to tune.

matt: thanks — if we get this right we can cut cold-start token latency by a solid margin. :rocket:

lee: ditto. also let's add some end-to-end tests: simulate NFS+S3 combos and random failures.

anika: cool. will post follow-up with rough manifest YAML and test matrix. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
